# ADO701: shellcheck

ShellCheck finding in an inline bash script.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Category** | Scripts |
| **Default severity** | per finding (the tool's own severity) |
| **Enabled by default** | yes |
| **Checked on** | ShellCheck, run on inline bash scripts extracted from the expanded pipeline |

## Description

Inline bash scripts are checked with ShellCheck. This covers bash steps, script steps on Linux and macOS pools, and the Bash@3 and AzureCLI@2 tasks. Findings are reported as ADO701/SCxxxx with ShellCheck's severity. Template expressions and $(Var.Name) macros are replaced by same-length placeholders first. The recommended profile covers parse errors plus SC2046, SC2164, SC2155, SC2181 and SC2034 (SC2086, unquoted variables, is available with include or the all profile).

### Rule profile

The default `recommended` profile reports every SC1xxx parse error plus:

- [SC2046](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/SC2046)
- [SC2164](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/SC2164)
- [SC2155](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/SC2155)
- [SC2181](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/SC2181)
- [SC2034](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/SC2034)

These are never reported unless listed in `include`, because they misfire on pipeline scripts: `SC2154`, `SC1090`, `SC1091`.

Choose `all` or `none`, or adjust the set:

```yaml
scripts:
  shellcheck:
    profile: recommended   # recommended | all | none
    include: []
    exclude: []
```

Findings are reported as `ADO701/<code>`. Suppress one with `# adolint:disable-next-line ADO701/<code>` or with ShellCheck's own suppression syntax. ShellCheck runs from `PATH` and isn't bundled.

## Example

Problem:

```yaml
- bash: cd $(Build.SourcesDirectory)/app && rm -rf $DIR/*
```

Instead:

```yaml
- bash: |
    cd "$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/app" || exit 1
    rm -rf "${DIR:?}"/*
```

## Configuration

Change the severity or turn the rule off in `.adolint.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  ADO701: off   # off | info | warning | error
```

Or on the command line: `adolint lint --disable ADO701` or `--enable ADO701`.

Suppress a single finding with a comment on the line before it (or `disable-line` at the end of the line):

```yaml
# adolint:disable-next-line ADO701
```
